# Independent audit: simultaneous projective centroid boundary potential

Source: `candidate 2d9458b5433d0a83`.

Result: PASS with no correction identified. The source proves an ordinary
boundary-weight theorem for every convex body and every interior source,
not a projective transformation of a mixed body. The constructive erosion
is independently supplied in the companion gauge note.

## 1. Attainment and geometric normalization

The parameter domain is bounded by the fixed inradius. The supporting
point x0 at a limiting domain-boundary parameter is transverse to its
orthogonal hyperplane. Consequently the displayed cone has a genuinely
positive Jacobian factor. Integrating its t-shell from delta to2delta
gives volume of order delta^d and integrand bounded below by a constant
times delta^(-d-1), so the required blowup is1/delta. This covers d=1
with a zero-dimensional disk as stated. Compact sublevels, an attained
unique minimum, and differentiation at an interior minimizer all follow.

The projective Jacobian exponent d+1 and centroid exponent d+2 check
exactly. Positive denominators preserve oriented central halfspaces,
convexity, and compactness. No lattice-preserving claim is needed or made.

## 2. Potential and exact boundary identity

The tangent continuation below the positive denominator minimum is
globally finite, positive and C1, with nondecreasing derivative. It is
therefore an admissible convex-in-x function even outside the source
body; this avoids an otherwise substantive inverse-power-domain gap.

The divergence of x/(1+a.x)^d is exactly d/(1+a.x)^(d+1).
Its boundary flux is the displayed h_K(n) weight. The new cap-plane flux
vanishes because the plane passes through the translated source. The
original-boundary intersection with that plane has surface measure zero,
as a relative section boundary, so closed cap conventions are retained.
Convex bodies are Lipschitz domains; smoothness or strict convexity is
not required for this flux identity. The d=1 endpoint calculation has
the same normalization with H0.

I also derived the identity independently by radial area formula in the
gauge-erosion companion: both sides equal the sphere integral of
rho(u)^d/(1+a.rho(u)u)^d over the same hemisphere. Thus the boundary
exponent d, rather than the interior exponent d+1, is correct.

## 3. Constant and simultaneous quantifiers

Ordinary centroid Grunbaum on the one actual centroid-zero projective
image yields exactly Gamma_d. The positive boundary weight then extends
the conclusion from through-source caps to every containing closed cap.
One fixed potential works for all caps and all nonnegative profile weights
before any circuit is selected. This conclusion does not follow from the
old section-minimum invariant alone; the new ingredient is the exact
weighted boundary identity, now proved.

The archive search found the normalization and separate projective
transport obstructions, but no earlier simultaneous boundary-weight or
gauge-erosion conclusion. Those obstructions compare different quantities
and do not refute this identity. The source properly retains the unresolved
anchored-contact compatibility interface, d=0 exclusion, and intrinsic
measure limitations.
